title: Special Right Triangles: Recognize, Scale, Solve
description: Recognize 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles from ratios, keywords, and common geometry setups, then find every side from any numeric or variable side.

questions.stem_html: A square’s diagonal is \(8\sqrt2\). What is its side length?
questions.explanation_html: The diagonal forms a 45–45–90 triangle with two square sides. Its length is the side times √2, so the side is 8.
questions.variation: Recover the side of a square using its diagonal

questions.stem_html: An equilateral triangle has altitude \(6\sqrt3\). What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation_html: The altitude splits the equilateral triangle into two 30–60–90 triangles. The long leg is 6√3, so the short leg is 6. The original side is 12 and the perimeter is 36.
questions.variation: Recover an equilateral triangle’s side and perimeter from its altitude

questions.stem_html: In a 30°–60°–90° triangle the side opposite the 60° angle has length \(9\sqrt3\). What is the hypotenuse length?
questions.explanation_html: The long leg is the short leg multiplied by √3, making the short leg 9. The hypotenuse is twice that length.
questions.variation: Recover the hypotenuse from the longer leg

questions.stem_html: Two radii of a circle meet at a right angle. The distance between the two endpoints on the circle is \(7\sqrt2\). What is the radius?
questions.explanation_html: The radii form equal perpendicular legs. The chord connecting their endpoints is the hypotenuse and equals the radius times √2.
questions.variation: Find a radius using a special triangle inside a circle

questions.stem_html: A right triangle has a 30° angle and a short leg of length \(4t\), where t is positive. Which expression gives the side opposite the 60° angle?
questions.explanation_html: The 30–60–90 side ratio is 1:√3:2. The long leg equals the short leg multiplied by √3.
questions.variation: Apply the same ratio to a variable side length
